title: Zone Cooperative Shedding Protocol (ZCSP) — multi-region coordinated admission + graceful fidelity fallbacks
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: During cross-region traffic spikes and partial failures we observe noisy neighbor effects and cascading latency that burn global error budgets. Existing per-node admission controllers make locally-optimal decisions that can amplify imbalances across zones (one zone sheds aggressively while another absorbs excess traffic and then overloads).

Objectives:
- Provide a cooperative multi-region load-shedding mechanism that preserves per-zone SLOs while minimizing global request loss and cost.
- Support graceful, observable degradation modes (response trimming, fallback model, compressed output) rather than hard rejections when possible.
- Integrate with existing circuit breaker and error-budget plumbing and expose control knobs for Dedicated/Private customers.

Design summary (Zone Cooperative Shedding Protocol - ZCSP):
1) Two-tier decision model:
   - Fast local admission: per-node, latency-first admission gate using token-bucket scaled by tenant weight and a short-term headroom estimate. This ensures sub-ms decisions on the hot path.
   - Soft global coordination: zone agents periodically (every 500–2000ms, adaptive) gossip summarized headroom and recent burn rates to neighboring zones and the control plane. Zones adopt a "soft adjustment" multiplier to their local token buckets based on neighbors' headroom to reduce oscillation.
2) Client-provided fidelity hints: SDKs can send an optional "x-redwood-fidelity" header with tolerance (low/medium/high) and preferred degradation strategies (truncate_tokens, compress_json, fallback_model). The admission layer uses this to choose a degradation path instead of rejecting when feasible.
3) Graded degradation ladder: on soft-shed decisions, the node attempts actions in order until cost/latency targets are met: (a) prefix cache boost / reuse, (b) KV cache warm-path, (c) response trimming (drop optional fields, reduce token budget), (d) switch to a lower-cost quantized model variant, (e) return terse fallback response (status + short message), (f) reject.
4) Circuit breaker integration: CBs operate at tenant and zone levels. When a tenant crosses its error budget threshold we move it into a protected mode where only essential requests are allowed; in protected mode we prefer degradation to rejections.
5) Cross-region failover policy: control plane maintains a regional preference order and capacity score. When a zone's headroom falls below the failover threshold for more than T seconds, the control plane issues a temporary multi-region routing hint (best-effort) to upstream routers and SDKs.

Config knobs and telemetry:
- zone_headroom: float (0..1)
- coordination_interval_ms: 500-2000
- local_token_bucket_rate: tokens/sec per tenant class
- fidelity_priority_order: list
- cb_error_budget_pct: %
Telemetry emitted:
- shed_decisions_total (tags: zone, tenant, reason, degradation_step)
- degrade_success_rate (how often degradation met latency targets)
- headroom_estimate_{zone} (gauge)
- error_budget_burn_rate (tenant/zone)
- p99_latency_post_degradation

Why different: ZCSP aims to be cooperative (soft multipliers from neighboring zones), prioritizes graceful fidelity reductions via client hints, and explicitly ties to routing hints for multi-region failover instead of only local eviction. This is a governance-level change (node + zone + control-plane) rather than a purely local shedder prototype.
acceptance_criteria: Implement local admission gate with token-bucket and per-tenant weights and expose zone_headroom metric
Implement gossip/coordination agent that emits soft multipliers and a control-plane reconciliation endpoint
Degradation ladder implemented with safe fallbacks in runtime: response trimming, model variant fallback, compressed payloads
Client SDK accepts x-redwood-fidelity header and behavior is respected end-to-end in canary tests
End-to-end test: under injected cross-region spike, observed global error budget burn reduced by >=30% compared to baseline and global P99 tail reduced by >=15%
Runbook updated with clear operator actions and circuit breaker transitions
Feature behind runtime feature flag + control-plane rollout gates with canary by region
comments: 2026-02-22 — Aisha Patel: Initial design sketch shared with Reliability and Runtime teams. Key risk: coordination chatter could add overhead during extreme bursts. We discussed adaptive intervals and summarization to keep messages small.

2026-03-02 — Marco Li: Prototype for local admission gate done (branch: github.com/redwood-inference/zcs-proto). Local tests show <0.5ms median decision latency. Pushed telemetry hooks for headroom and shed_decisions_total.

2026-03-05 — Design review notes (from Priya Kaur): recommend adding an explicit safety valve to disable soft coordination if network latency between zones is high. Also asked for stronger typing for fidelity header values and a SDK feature flag.

2026-03-09 — Perf team: synthetic multi-region spike (10x normal) run: preliminary results show 22% reduction in cross-zone tail compared to baseline when soft multipliers enabled. Need longer runs and tenant-mix workloads.

2026-03-12 — Security review requested: we confirmed fidelity header is optional and sanitized; control-plane endpoints require mTLS. Marked security_review_required: true for final rollout. (Action: Security team to complete by 2026-03-20)

2026-03-14 — Marco Li: Merged PR implementing graded degradation ladder into canary runtime (PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/6249). Next: wire control-plane reconciliation and SDK hint support. Added integration test plan in attachments.
risks_and_mitigation:
Risk: Over-coordination can create feedback loops leading to oscillation. Mitigation: conservative soft multipliers, backoff on coordination during high churn, and operator kill-switch.
Risk: SDK adoption delay could reduce graceful fallbacks. Mitigation: server-side default fidelity behavior and gradual rollout.
Risk: Incorrect degradation could affect output quality. Mitigation: per-tenant policy to opt-out of aggressive fidelity steps for high-sensitivity customers.
rollout_plan: 1) Merge canary runtime with feature flag off. 2) Enable local admission gate in single non-prod region, run chaos. 3) Enable graded degradation ladder in canary region and exercise with synthetic tests. 4) Enable soft coordination between two regions and monitor headroom and p99. 5) Gradually increase regions and flip control-plane gate. 6) Enable SDK header on staged clients and monitor degrade_success_rate. 7) Full rollout once metrics and runbook checks pass.
test_plan:
- Unit tests for token-bucket, soft multiplier math, and degradation selector.
- Integration test: two-zone sim with latent link and tenant-mix to validate reduction in tail.
- Chaos test: drop inter-zone coordination messages and ensure system stays stable.
- Customer regression test: run a subset of customer prompt sets through degradation ladder to measure quality drop and false negatives.
- Smoke test: enable and disable feature flag quickly to ensure no state corruption.
notes: Prefer to keep client fidelity header opt-in; default server-side behavior will attempt a conservative trim if header absent. Coordinate with SDK/Docs for migration.
